BEAM subtlety the untimed model hides: any message resets a GenServer timeout, including :sys.get_state polls. The driver never saw the timeout until it stopped polling. In the model a timeout may fire regardless, which is the safe direction
nodes.description: Untimed timers over-approximate: the model admits a timeout firing after a pong. The real system under-fires when the mailbox is busy. Safety proofs hold in both; liveness of the watchdog (a hung worker is eventually replaced) would need the timer to actually fire, i.e. a fairness assumption on timers plus quiet mailboxes.

Defer clause and loop_tail semantics: a loop module with no unguarded bare-pattern clause gets '| me, _, .<mod> s_0.., m => (.<mod> s_0.., [.send me m])' after its last clause; tail 'f(e)' -> {:noreply, e}, 'exit(r)' kept, statement kept then exit(:normal), plain value -> exit(:normal); rewriting descends through if/case

Why it matters: this is the encoding of selective receive; the re-enqueue delivers to self, so the message count of the process is preserved and the proof must frame it (mcount_deliver). The explorer never sends start/EXIT to a worker, so the defer clause does not enlarge the explored state space; it is exercised by beh_eq_gen and the SupervisorProof cases, not by the checker.

nodes.description: NOTES section 6, replace the bullet "Exit reasons collapse to normal | error ... under-approximation" with: "Exit reasons are normal, error and kill. Process.exit(p, :kill) is the untrappable kill it is on the BEAM: the target dies whatever it traps and its links and monitors see error (:killed). A remote Process.exit(p, :normal) is ignored by a non-trapping target and is an EXIT message to a trapping one. nodes.title: Semantics of the generation encoding and its remaining approximations
nodes.description: Exact w.r.t. the BEAM for processed messages: a receive entry arms exactly one live timer (generation = state gen) and any message handled by an arm cancels it by moving to gen+1, so a stale after_<loop> (carried gen != state gen) is consumed and ignored (`stale_ignored` in TtlProof). Two things remain approximations, both towards more behaviours: (1) timers are still untimed, so the live timer may fire before or after any message; (2) the defer clause and a failed guard re-enter at gen+1 and arm a fresh timer, whereas the BEAM keeps the original timeout running when it skips a non-matching message (the model can delay the expiry across skipped messages; it cannot produce an expiry the BEAM could not, because the fresh timer may fire immediately). The old accumulation approximation (a stale after firing late after other messages were handled) is gone. Lean has no non-linear patterns, so the stale-ignore is the else branch of the after clause (`| me, _, .cache v gen, .after_run gen' => if gen' = gen then ... else (.cache v gen, [])`), placed before the defer clause; it is not a separate Lean clause. Timers still accumulate in Sys.timers (stale entries stay until fired); no timer-cancel effect was added to Sys.lean. Checker counts: explore beh sig init 7 3 = 16,723 (was 17,206), mutant behNoRaise caught after 29 configurations: timer 0, run 0, timer 0, run 0, env put 0 -> 0, run 0 (two live expiries then put 0). Stage A ranks the pending (0, c, _) signal by its position in the FIFO queue (a run only appends signals, a signal step pops the head), stage B ranks EXIT c _ by its position in the supervisor mailbox (every other step only appends to it, run 0 pops the head and either spawns or leaves the state alone).
